subject: guys named Steve
one_liner: The coffee chain where the barista gets your name right on the first try. It's Steve. We checked at the door.
brand_voice_notes: Speaks like a regional operations manager who has read one book about hospitality. Treats the name Steve as a supply-chain efficiency, not a joke. Every name-related problem is solved with more process. Never acknowledges that a coffee shop for one first name is strange. Stephens, Stevens and Stefans are a compliance matter, handled politely and slowly.

hero.h1: We already wrote your name on the cup.
hero.sub: Stevedore is a coffee chain for one customer segment: guys named Steve. Every cup ships pre-printed. Every order is called once. Seven Steves answer, and we have a process for that.

features.title: Pre-printed cups
features.blurb: Every cup leaves the factory reading STEVE in our house marker hand. Baristas no longer ask, spell, or guess. Bar throughput is up 41% since we removed the question.

features.title: Door-side Steve verification
features.blurb: Two forms of Steve ID at the threshold. A driver's licence and a coworker who can confirm it. Stephens are admitted under review. Stevens with an n are processed in the order received.

features.title: The Descriptor Engine
features.blurb: When we call 'Steve' and nine men stand up, the Descriptor Engine assigns each order a visible attribute at the till. Steve (Blue Fleece). Steve (Has Kayak On Car). Steve (Second Steve From Accounts). Collisions resolved in under four seconds.

testimonials.quote: For eleven years I was 'Stove', 'Steph' and once 'Sieve'. Here they called me Steve before I opened my mouth. I sat in the car for a minute afterwards.
testimonials.name: Steve Okafor
testimonials.title: Regional Logistics Lead, Second Steve In His Office

testimonials.quote: The Descriptor Engine assigned me 'Steve (Clearly Retired)'. It was right. I have upgraded to Prime so I can change it to 'Steve (Consultant)'.
testimonials.name: Steve Lindqvist
testimonials.title: Former Orthodontist, Goes By Steve, Has Always Gone By Steve

testimonials.quote: My application has been under review since March. The coffee in the waiting area is very good. I am told the Council meets in November.

testimonials.title: Applicant, Spelled With A V, Status Pending

demo_screen_concept: The Stevedore barista console during the 8:40am rush. A live order rail of nine tickets, every one for 'Steve', each with a small headshot, drink, wait timer and an assigned descriptor chip like 'Blue Fleece' or 'Has Kayak'. Filter chips narrow the rail by descriptor family (outerwear, vehicle, workplace). Pressing 'Call Steve' fires the call and a collision meter shows how many Steves stood up; the Disambiguation modal then lets the barista reassign a descriptor before calling again. A side tab holds the Door Verification queue of pending Stephens and Stevens with approve, defer and 'refer to Council' buttons.

images.rationale: Retail cafe direction calls for a lifestyle hero, so one hero photo of a Steve at the counter. Three testimonial headshots (the subject is a type of person, so faces carry the bit); the demo order rail reuses those headshots as queue avatars and fills the other six tickets with initials badges, so no separate demo assets were spent.

design_direction.style: Kraft-cup café retail with a conference name-tag layer, morning daylight mode. The page is staged as the counter of a coffee chain that runs like a trade show registration desk: kraft-paper cups, the red HELLO MY NAME IS badge, a loyalty punch card and the thermal ticket that prints at the bar. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: conflict markers, gutter stripes, data strips, viewfinder brackets, contours, thumbnail circles and arrows, highlighter swipes, VHS labels, OSD menus, tracking lines, 24-hour bars, Swiss grids, giant numerals, candlelight, foil rules, menu leaders, LED-lime accents. Also absent: dark mode, glassmorphism, neon, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The name tag: section headers sit inside a badge with a red top band reading in small caps and a white writing area below. (2) The cup scrawl: the word STEVE, and only that word, is set in Permanent Marker, slightly rotated, like a barista's hand. (3) The punch card: progress and pricing perks are rows of 10 circles, punched ones filled in espresso. (4) The ticket: drink orders, prices and timers sit on a narrow thermal-receipt strip with a zigzag torn bottom edge, set in mono. Corners 10px on badges, 0 on tickets. Shadows are a single soft 0 2px 0 kraft drop.

fonts.body: 'Work Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Feature-rich retail showcase: hero with product photo, three-feature badge row, testimonials as name tags, pricing as punch cards
design_direction.motion_vocab: Badges settle with a 2deg wobble on hover. The STEVE scrawl draws in once on load via a clip-path wipe. Ticket strips slide up 8px when they enter. Everything 180-260ms ease-out, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: a HELLO MY NAME IS badge whose writing area holds the scrawled STEVE, then the h1 in Archivo Black, the sub, and a red CTA plus a ticket-strip stat ('Steves served today 4,112'). Right: the hero photo cropped tall-ish in a kraft frame with a thermal ticket pinned over its lower-left corner. Stacks on mobile with the photo second.
